thread:
incbot: ALERT: spike in 5xx/504 observed for region eu-central-2 (gw-euc2-1)
incbot: summary: overall 5xx = 8.1% (baseline ~0.2%), 504 = 4.0%, p50 latency from ~120ms -> ~1s
incbot: affected endpoint(s): /v1/generate (hosted) -> model pool: redwood-ggml-quantized-1
incbot: suggested checks: NAT/egress saturation, gateway conn pools, cbreaks, failover rules

pagerduty: paging jess (oncall) -> critical. escalation to eng-sre in 4m if not acked

jess (oncall): acked. Triaging now. tagging eng-sre, eng-runtime, and eng-infra. Who has recent gw logs?

mia: pulling logs and metrics now. running quick query:
```
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?cluster=gw-euc2-1&window=10m" | jq '.http.errors'
```
mia: quick values: http_5xx:0.081, http_504:0.04, conn_reset:0.025

sanju: egress-proxy in euc2 shows connection_pool_exhausted spikes. nat-gw nodes reporting ~63k connections against a 64k soft limit. churn from many short-lived inference sessions. no deploys in last 3h per deploy-bot.

kevin: control-plane looks green but router-worker on egress-proxy-euc2-3 at 94% CPU. kernel backlog and repeated logs: "Upstream connection reset by peer" and "connect timeout to model-host-1:443"

anya: product wants an impact estimate for customers and whether any reserved-capacity tenants were affected.

product-oncall: preliminary: ~1.2k reqs/min failing during peak; mostly free-tier/low-priority hosted traffic. 3 enterprise tenants saw latency but were served by reserved pools fallback. No data loss reported.

lucas: we have a policy to steer non-SLA traffic to eu-west-1. we can flip selective failover for low-priority /v1/generate now.

ops-lead: suggested immediate mitigations:
1) enable selective failover for low-priority /v1/generate to eu-west-1
2) scale egress-proxy pool in euc2 (hot scale)
3) rotate offending NAT node(s) to relieve connection limits
4) monitor and prepare rollback if regressions

jess (oncall): agree. Mia, run the route update and paste command + rollout id. want traceable audit.

mia: running route update:
```
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate --region eu-central-2 --fallback eu-west-1 --selector priority=low --enable
```
mia: response: route-change accepted, rollout=rl_2026_1765559999, status=rolling

incbot: Action registered: routing update submitted by mia. Edge propagation may take 20-45s. Watching metrics.

(30s)

mia: metrics after rollout t+45s: 5xx -> 3.4%, 504 -> 1.8%. Traffic to eu-west-1 for /v1/generate low-priority increased ~20%. Partial mitigation visible.

sanju: initiating nat rotate on nat-euc2-4:
```
infractl nat rotate --node nat-euc2-4 --drain --timeout 300
```
sanju: drain complete, new nat-euc2-6 provisioned and attached. conn resets reduced but not zero.

kevin: scaling egress-proxy pool (hotfix):
```
infractl scale pool egress-proxy-euc2 --replicas +2 --reason "incident 1765559999"
```
kevin: pods scheduling; worker CPU dropping to ~70% after new pods are up. backlog clearing.

product-oncall: customer impact summary for ops: total failed ~12k requests in 25m window. Enterprise SLAs: 3 tenants saw increased latency but requests served via reserved capacity, no SLA breaches detected so far. Public endpoints degraded during spike.

jess (oncall): temporary plan: keep selective failover for 60 minutes, re-evaluate. revert only if 5xx < 0.5% sustained for 30m. Opening incident channel for postmortem/owners.

ops-lead: RCA focus: why NAT pools saturated? look at connection churn patterns, short-lived TLS sessions, lack of connection reuse. Assign to eng-runtime to evaluate batching/keepalive improvements.

lucas: proposing follow-up: lower per-host concurrency defaults in euc2 routing policy to reduce peak NAT connection usage. will draft change and run impact simulation.

anya: preparing customer comms and support tickets. Draft status to CS: "We observed elevated errors in eu-central-2 gateway between 17:45-18:10 UTC. Traffic was partially rerouted and systems are stabilizing. We will follow up with a post-incident summary."

incbot: MONITOR UPDATE t+12m: 5xx = 0.6%, 504 = 0.2%. trend stable but still monitoring for regressions.

jess (oncall): handing active incident to kevin (secondary oncall). I'm going offline but reachable. Kevin, you have control-plane ownership for next shift.

kevin: taking over. logging notes to incident doc rl_2026_1765559999. running deeper heap/profile on egress proxies, creating follow-up tickets: NAT-autoscale, connection-reuse, routing-tuning.

anya: filing outreach tasks for CS + SRE-led incident summary. will coordinate triage notes and timeline.

incbot: AUTO RESOLVE CHECK suggests maintain selective failover for 30 more minutes. Manual close after team sign-off and timeline captured.

kevin: leaving failover in place for 30m then gradually drain back. current status: mitigated -> monitoring.

jess (oncall): thanks team, great response :thumbsup:

---
Post-incident summary lines (for postmortem):
- Symptom: NAT/egress connection exhaustion in eu-central-2 causing upstream connection resets and connect timeouts -> spike in 5xx/504 and latency degradation.
- Immediate mitigations: selective failover of low-priority /v1/generate traffic to eu-west-1; scaled egress-proxy pool; rotated NAT node.
- Impact: mostly low-priority requests; ~12k failed requests; 3 enterprise tenants experienced degraded latency but remained served by reserved capacity.
- Follow-ups: enable NAT autoscale, improve connection reuse/keepalive, tune routing concurrency defaults, produce postmortem and customer communications.
